A DJ plays recorded music for people, one track flowing into the next. The job needs two (or more) sources you can start, stop and
speed up independently, and a **mixer** to blend them, with headphones to hear the next track before anyone else does.

## The decks

- **Turntables**. The Technics SL-1200 (1972 onwards) became the club standard: a direct-drive motor that gets to speed in under a
  second, a heavy platter, and a **pitch fader** (±8 %, later ±16 % on some models). A **slipmat** lets the record slip over the
  spinning platter, so you can hold the record still while the platter turns, then let go on the beat.
- **CDJs** (Pioneer's name, now used for all such players) play files from USB sticks. A **jog wheel** stands in for the record:
  touch the top to scratch, turn the side to nudge. Tempo range, cue and loop buttons, **key lock** (Master Tempo) and a waveform display.
- **DVS** (digital vinyl systems): turntables playing records of a timecode signal that software reads, so a laptop file follows the
  record's speed and direction. Serato, rekordbox and Traktor all offer it with supported audio interfaces.
- **Controllers**: two jog wheels, a mixer and pads in one box, for DJ software on a laptop. Cheaper and lighter; the same skills.

## The mixer

Each **channel** has, top to bottom: **gain** (trim the input so loud and quiet tracks match), **EQ** (usually three bands: high,
mid, low, cutting well below the boost, so a band can be nearly "killed"), often a **filter**, a **cue** button (send this channel to
the headphones), and the **channel fader**. Then the **crossfader** blends the two sides, and the **master** sets the output level.

- **Headphones**: the **cue mix** (or "cue/master") knob blends what you've cued with the master. Some DJs use **split cue**: cue in
  one ear, master in the other.
- **Crossfader curve**: smooth (both sides at full in the middle, for long blends) or sharp (a cut, for scratching: the sound comes
  in within a millimetre of the edge).

## Your decks

The widget below is the practice rig for these lessons: two decks and a two-channel mixer. Everything here works with a mouse or
a finger.

<div class="dj-tt" data-id="dj-gear" data-a="demo:house124" data-b="demo:disco118"></div>

1. Press **▶** on deck A. Notice the platter turning, the waveform scrolling past the red line (now), and the time readout.
2. **Stop** and start it again: the "motor" takes a moment to reach speed and to stop, as a real turntable does.
3. Pull the **Lo** knob on channel A all the way down: the kick and bass vanish. Bring it back.
4. Move the **crossfader** from A to B, with deck B playing. Then press **CUE** on channel B, and click **Listen: speakers** to switch
   to what the headphones would hear. A browser has one output, so this is how you hear the cue here; with **Split cue** ticked and
   headphones on, cue is in the left ear and the master in the right.
5. Drag the **label** of a playing record: you are holding it. Move it back and forth. Then drag the **rim** (the outer ring) while
   it plays: the side of the platter, to speed it up or slow it down a touch (a **nudge**).

## Choosing gear

| | Turntables + mixer | CDJs + mixer | Controller |
|---|---|---|---|
| Music | Records (or DVS) | USB / SD files, streaming | Files on a laptop, streaming |
| Cost | High | Highest | Lowest |
| In clubs | Some, for vinyl nights and scratch DJs | The standard booth | Rare in booths; common for mobile DJs |
| Learn here | All of it | All of it | All of it |

Start with whatever you have. Beatmatching, phrasing and EQ are the same on all of them.

## In other gear

<div class="dj-map">

| | [Serato DJ Pro](https://serato.com/dj/pro/downloads) | [rekordbox](https://rekordbox.com/en/download/) | [Traktor Pro](https://www.native-instruments.com/en/support/downloads/) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Load a track | Drag from the library to a deck | Drag to a deck, or the deck's Load | Drag to a deck |
| Pitch range | Tempo range ±8/16/50 % in the deck | Tempo range ±6/10/16 %/WIDE | Tempo range in Preferences |
| Key lock | KEYLOCK | MASTER TEMPO | Keylock |
| Headphone cue | Cue buttons in the mixer, Cue mix | CUE, Headphones MIX | Cue buttons, Mix knob |
| Timecode vinyl (DVS) | Serato DJ Pro with DVS | rekordbox DVS | Traktor Scratch |

</div>

The manuals are on each program's download page (Serato DJ Pro manual, rekordbox Operating Instructions, Traktor Pro manual).
